# Supplementary Figure 7

## Getting the data

Processed data are deposited at ArrayExpress, genome assemblies at ENA:

| Data | Accession |
|---|---|
| Single-nucleus RNA-seq | `E-MTAB-17757` |
| Single-nucleus ATAC-seq | `E-MTAB-17776` |
| Genome assemblies | `PRJEB115767` |

Everything except the single-nucleus atlases is committed in this repository
under `data/reference/`: orthology maps, TF lists, SAMap scores, gene-to-GO
maps, TF activity, the differential expression tables and the SCENIC+ output.

Only the atlases need downloading. Put them in one folder and point
`DATA_DIR` at it; the files are used exactly as ArrayExpress delivers them, so
nothing needs renaming.

```
<DATA_DIR>/
`-- snRNA/
    `-- seurat/                                  E-MTAB-17757
        |-- BifurcaAtlas.rds
        |-- BrachiAtlas.rds
        |-- FormosaAtlas.rds
        |-- GracilisAtlas_pregnant_non_pregnant.rds
        |-- GracilisAtlas_pregnant.rds
        |-- InfansAtlas.rds
        |-- PhallocerusAtlas.rds
        |-- PictaAtlas.rds
        |-- ProlificaAtlas.rds
        |-- TurneriAtlas_pregnant_non_pregnant_juvenile.rds
        `-- TurneriAtlas_pregnant.rds
```

Panels use the combined atlas for *P. gracilis* and *P. turneri* unless stated
otherwise; Figure 1B uses the pregnant-only *P. turneri* atlas.

Every atlas carries a `cell_type` column, which the scripts use rather than
per-species cluster numbers.

SPECIES <- c("gracilis", "turneri", "bifurca", "picta")

                                     paste0(sp, "_activity_df.rds"))

```{r activity-matrices}
## PURPOSE : Read per-species TF motif activity: motif enrichment in each cell type's marker peaks.
## PRODUCES: activity_dfs - one motif x cell type matrix per species

# TF activity: motif enrichment in each cell type's marker peaks, as -log10
# adjusted p-values. Read, not recomputed: the deposited ArchR projects keep
# the motif match files but their peakAnnotation slot is empty, so
# peakAnnoEnrichment() cannot be run against them.

activity_dfs <- lapply(SPECIES, function(sp) {
  f <- activity_f(sp)
  if (!file.exists(f)) stop("missing activity table: ", f, call. = FALSE)
  as.data.frame(readRDS(f))
})
names(activity_dfs) <- SPECIES

lapply(activity_dfs, colnames)
```

# A. Cross-species TF-activity similarity

```{r merge}
## PURPOSE : Reduce the four species to the motifs scored in all of them, dropping embryonic cell types and invariant motifs.
## PRODUCES: merged_df_filtered
## QUESTION: none - puts the four species on a common set of motifs.

# One matrix of species_cellType columns, over the motifs scored in all four,
# without the embryonic cell types or invariant motifs.
common_tfs <- Reduce(intersect, lapply(activity_dfs, rownames))
message("motifs scored in all four species: ", length(common_tfs))

merged_df <- do.call(cbind, lapply(SPECIES, function(sp) {
  d <- activity_dfs[[sp]][common_tfs, , drop = FALSE]
  colnames(d) <- paste(sp, colnames(d), sep = "_")
  d
}))

# embryonic cell types are present in only some species and dominate the
# clustering if kept
merged_df <- merged_df[, !grepl("Embryonic", colnames(merged_df))]

rv <- apply(merged_df, 1, var)
merged_df_filtered <- merged_df[is.finite(rv) & rv > 0, , drop = FALSE]

dim(merged_df_filtered)
```

```{r similarity-helpers}
## PURPOSE : Define Pearson similarity within and between activity matrices.
## PRODUCES: simMat() and the between-matrix helper
## QUESTION: none - analysis helper.

# Pearson similarity, within one matrix and between two.
METHOD <- "pearson"

simMat <- function(x, method = METHOD) {
  s <- cor(as.matrix(x), method = method, use = "pairwise.complete.obs")
  s[is.na(s)] <- 0
  s
}

crossSim <- function(a, b, method = METHOD) {
  s <- cor(as.matrix(a), as.matrix(b), method = method)
  s[is.na(s)] <- 0
  s
}

scaleFor <- function(method = METHOD) {
  list(col = colorRampPalette(c("blue", "white", "red"))(100),
       brk = seq(-1, 1, length.out = 101))
}

species_colors <- c(turneri = "#377EB8", gracilis = "#E41A1C",
                    bifurca = "#4DAF4A", picta = "#FF7F00")
```

## A1. Global similarity, every cell type in every species

```{r sf7a-global, fig.width = 13, fig.height = 12}
## PURPOSE : Supplementary 7A - cluster every species-by-cell-type column on TF activity.
## PRODUCES: the heatmap, printed in the document
## QUESTION: do the same cell types group across species, or does each species group with itself?

# Supplementary 7A: do the same cell types group across species, or does each
# species group with itself?
s  <- simMat(merged_df_filtered)
sc <- scaleFor()

ann <- data.frame(Species  = sub("_.*", "", colnames(s)),
                  CellType = sub("^[^_]*_", "", colnames(s)),
                  row.names = colnames(s))
ctPal <- setNames(colorRampPalette(brewer.pal(8, "Set2"))(length(unique(ann$CellType))),
                  sort(unique(ann$CellType)))

# annotation_col only: the matrix is symmetric, and annotating both axes draws
# the species and cell-type legends twice. ComplexHeatmap's pheatmap takes the
# same arguments and lets the colour legend be named.
if (requireNamespace("ComplexHeatmap", quietly = TRUE)) {
  ComplexHeatmap::pheatmap(
    s,
    name = "Pearson correlation",
    main = "Global TF-activity similarity",
    clustering_method = "ward.D2",
    annotation_col = ann,
    annotation_colors = list(Species = species_colors, CellType = ctPal),
    color = sc$col, breaks = sc$brk,
    show_rownames = FALSE, fontsize_col = 6)
} else {
  pheatmap(s,
           main = "Global TF-activity similarity (Pearson correlation)",
           clustering_method = "ward.D2",
           annotation_col = ann,
           annotation_colors = list(Species = species_colors, CellType = ctPal),
           color = sc$col, breaks = sc$brk,
           show_rownames = FALSE, fontsize_col = 6)
}
```

# B. Transcription factors with shared patterns across species

```{r sf7b-pipelines}
## PURPOSE : Rank TFs by the two activity patterns of interest.
## PRODUCES: the per-pattern TF rankings
## QUESTION: which TFs peak in granulosa and theca, and which in the late follicle cell?

# TFs whose activity ranks follow one of two patterns: top in granulosa and
# theca, or focused on the late follicle cell. Ranks are taken over these cell
# types only, and are natural ranks - no per-species activity floor.
PATTERN_CELL_TYPES <- c("Stromal", "Endothelial", "Vascular smooth muscle", "Immune",
                        "Erythrocytes", "Yolk pericardial sac", "Germinal epithelium",
                        "Late follicle cell", "Granulosa", "Theca")

# shared first steps: active in at least three cell types, and the third and
# fourth ranked clearly separated
rank_by_cell_type <- function(activity_df, min_gap = 3) {
  calc_df <- activity_df[, sapply(activity_df, is.numeric), drop = FALSE]
  calc_df <- calc_df[, intersect(PATTERN_CELL_TYPES, colnames(calc_df)), drop = FALSE]

  filtered_df <- calc_df[apply(calc_df, 1, function(row) sum(row > 2)) >= 3, , drop = FALSE]
  if (nrow(filtered_df) == 0) return(NULL)

  clear <- apply(filtered_df, 1, function(row) {
    srt <- sort(row, decreasing = TRUE)
    if (length(srt) >= 4) (srt[3] - srt[4]) >= min_gap else TRUE
  })
  filtered_df <- filtered_df[clear, , drop = FALSE]
  if (nrow(filtered_df) == 0) return(NULL)

  t(apply(filtered_df, 1, function(row) rank(-row, ties.method = "min")))
}

as_long <- function(matched_matrix, pattern_labels, species_name) {
  as.data.frame(matched_matrix) %>% rownames_to_column("TF") %>%
    mutate(Pattern = pattern_labels, Species = species_name) %>%
    pivot_longer(-c(TF, Pattern, Species), names_to = "CellType", values_to = "Rank")
}

# Pipeline 1: granulosa and theca together, or germinal epithelium first
find_dual_pattern_tfs_1 <- function(activity_df, species_name, min_gap = 3) {
  tf_rank <- rank_by_cell_type(activity_df, min_gap); if (is.null(tf_rank)) return(NULL)
  if (!all(c("Granulosa", "Theca", "Germinal epithelium") %in% colnames(tf_rank))) return(NULL)

  cond_g <- tf_rank[, "Granulosa"] %in% c(1, 2)
  cond_t <- tf_rank[, "Theca"] %in% c(1, 2)
  p1 <- unique(unlist(lapply(setdiff(colnames(tf_rank), c("Granulosa", "Theca")), function(cell) {
    idx <- cond_g & cond_t & tf_rank[, cell] == 3
    if (any(idx)) rownames(tf_rank)[idx] else NULL
  })))
  p2 <- rownames(tf_rank)[tf_rank[, "Germinal epithelium"] == 1 &
                          tf_rank[, "Granulosa"] %in% c(2, 3) &
                          tf_rank[, "Theca"] %in% c(2, 3)]

  all_tfs <- unique(c(p1, p2)); if (!length(all_tfs)) return(NULL)
  m <- tf_rank[all_tfs, , drop = FALSE]
  labels <- sapply(rownames(m), function(tf)
    paste(c(if (tf %in% p1) "Pattern 1 (granulosa/theca top 2)",
            if (tf %in% p2) "Pattern 2 (germinal epithelium first)"), collapse = " & "))
  as_long(m, labels, species_name)
}

# Pipeline 2: focused on the late follicle cell
find_dual_pattern_tfs_2 <- function(activity_df, species_name, min_gap = 3) {
  tf_rank <- rank_by_cell_type(activity_df, min_gap); if (is.null(tf_rank)) return(NULL)
  if (!all(c("Late follicle cell", "Germinal epithelium", "Granulosa", "Theca")
           %in% colnames(tf_rank))) return(NULL)

  p1 <- rownames(tf_rank)[tf_rank[, "Late follicle cell"] == 1]
  p2 <- rownames(tf_rank)[tf_rank[, "Late follicle cell"] == 2 &
                          tf_rank[, "Germinal epithelium"] == 1]

  all_tfs <- unique(c(p1, p2)); if (!length(all_tfs)) return(NULL)
  m <- tf_rank[all_tfs, , drop = FALSE]
  labels <- sapply(rownames(m), function(tf)
    paste(c(if (tf %in% p1) "A (late follicle cell first)",
            if (tf %in% p2) "B (late follicle second, germinal epithelium first)"),
          collapse = " & "))
  as_long(m, labels, species_name)
}
```

```{r sf7b-plots, fig.width = 18, fig.height = 9}
## PURPOSE : Supplementary 7B - mean activity rank per cell type across supporting species.
## PRODUCES: the two rank plots, printed in the document
## QUESTION: do the follicle lineages use distinguishable sets of regulators?

# Supplementary 7B: mean rank per cell type across the species that support a
# TF. A TF whose MEAN activity in a cell type is below act_floor is pushed to
# the bottom rank, so a low-activity cell type cannot look informative just
# because its rank happens to be high. Lines are offset slightly so overlapping
# TFs stay visible.
ACT_FLOOR <- 1

make_plot <- function(fn, title, subtitle, jitter = 0.35, act_floor = ACT_FLOOR) {
  n_ct <- length(PATTERN_CELL_TYPES)

  mc <- bind_rows(lapply(SPECIES, function(sp) fn(activity_dfs[[sp]], sp, min_gap = 3)))
  if (!nrow(mc)) { message("no TFs matched: ", title); return(invisible(NULL)) }

  # mean absolute activity per TF and cell type, across species
  act <- map_dfr(SPECIES, function(sp) {
    num <- as.matrix(activity_dfs[[sp]][, sapply(activity_dfs[[sp]], is.numeric), drop = FALSE])
    num <- num[, intersect(PATTERN_CELL_TYPES, colnames(num)), drop = FALSE]
    as.data.frame(num) %>% rownames_to_column("TF") %>%
      pivot_longer(-TF, names_to = "CellType", values_to = "Activity") %>%
      mutate(Species = sp)
  }) %>%
    group_by(TF, CellType) %>%
    summarise(Mean_Activity = mean(Activity, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop")

  consensus <- mc %>%
    group_by(TF, CellType) %>%
    summarise(Mean_Rank = mean(Rank, na.rm = TRUE),
              Species_Count = n_distinct(Species),
              Patterns_Matched = paste(unique(Pattern), collapse = " / "),
              .groups = "drop") %>%
    filter(Species_Count >= 2) %>%
    left_join(act, by = c("TF", "CellType")) %>%
    mutate(Mean_Rank = ifelse(!is.na(Mean_Activity) & Mean_Activity < act_floor,
                              n_ct, Mean_Rank))
  if (!nrow(consensus)) { message("nothing supported by two species: ", title); return(invisible(NULL)) }

  rank_table <- consensus %>%
    mutate(Mean_Rank = round(Mean_Rank, 2)) %>%
    dplyr::select(TF, CellType, Mean_Rank) %>%
    pivot_wider(names_from = CellType, values_from = Mean_Rank) %>%
    dplyr::select(TF, any_of(PATTERN_CELL_TYPES))

  activity_table <- consensus %>%
    mutate(Mean_Activity = round(Mean_Activity, 2)) %>%
    dplyr::select(TF, CellType, Mean_Activity) %>%
    pivot_wider(names_from = CellType, values_from = Mean_Activity) %>%
    dplyr::select(TF, any_of(PATTERN_CELL_TYPES))

  cat("\n==== ", title, " - mean rank per cell type ====\n")
  print(as.data.frame(rank_table), row.names = FALSE)
  cat("\n==== ", title, " - mean activity per cell type ====\n")
  print(as.data.frame(activity_table), row.names = FALSE)

  plot_df <- consensus %>%
    mutate(CellType = factor(CellType, levels = PATTERN_CELL_TYPES)) %>%
    filter(!is.na(CellType))

  tf_levels <- unique(plot_df$TF)
  offs <- setNames(seq(-jitter, jitter, length.out = max(length(tf_levels), 1)), tf_levels)
  plot_df$Rank_jit <- plot_df$Mean_Rank + offs[plot_df$TF]

  p <- ggplot(plot_df, aes(CellType, Rank_jit, group = TF, color = TF)) +
    geom_line(linewidth = 0.9, alpha = 0.7) +
    geom_point(aes(size = Species_Count), alpha = 0.85) +
    scale_y_reverse(breaks = seq(1, ceiling(max(plot_df$Mean_Rank)), by = 1)) +
    scale_size_continuous(breaks = 2:4, range = c(3, 6)) +
    theme_minimal() +
    theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1, face = "bold"),
          legend.position = "right", panel.grid.minor = element_blank()) +
    labs(title = title,
         subtitle = paste0(subtitle, " (mean activity < ", act_floor,
                           " forced to bottom rank; lines offset)"),
         x = "Cell type", y = "Mean rank", colour = "TF", size = "Species")
  print(p)
  invisible(list(ranks = rank_table, activity = activity_table, consensus = consensus))
}

invisible(make_plot(find_dual_pattern_tfs_1,
                    "Consensus TF signatures - granulosa and theca",
                    "Low mean activity forced to bottom rank"))

invisible(make_plot(find_dual_pattern_tfs_2,
                    "Consensus TF signatures - late follicle cell",
                    "Late follicle cell targeting"))
```
